cards.text: Jacob has put his wives and kids on camels, gathered all his flocks, and left his father-in-law Laban without telling him. On the way out, Rachel, Jacob's wife and Laban's daughter, stole her father's household idols. On the third day, somebody tells Laban that Jacob has fled.

cards.question: Laban just heard that Jacob is gone. What does Laban do?

answers.text: Takes his relatives and chases him
Sends his sons with a message
Lets him go and stays home

cards.text: Laban chases Jacob for SEVEN DAYS and catches up with him in the hill country of Gilead. Seven days, friend! I get winded hopping from one oven to the next, and my base does half the work.

cards.question: Laban is camped near Jacob in the hills of Gilead. That night, ___ comes to Laban in a dream.
In the dream, God warns Laban that he can say good things to Jacob, just nothing bad.

cards.text: With both camps pitched in the hills of Gilead, Laban confronts Jacob: “What have you done?” He says Jacob deceived him and carried off his daughters like captives of war.

cards.question: Laban says that if Jacob had just told him he was leaving, how would Laban have sent him off?

answers.text: With a guard of his men

cards.text: Tambourines AND harps, friend. Laban's planning the going-away party after the guest already left! And since Jacob didn't let him kiss his grandkids and daughters goodbye, Laban says Jacob has done a foolish thing.

cards.question: Laban tells Jacob he has the power to do him great harm. So why doesn't he?

answers.text: The God of Jacob's father warned him
His relatives talked him out of it
His daughters begged him not to

cards.text: Laban says he understands. Jacob left because he longs for his father's house. Then comes the big question.

cards.question: Laban asks Jacob why he has stolen Laban's ___.

cards.text: Jacob answers the first part: “I was afraid,” he says. He thought Laban would take his daughters from him by force.

cards.question: Now Jacob makes a bold promise about Laban's gods. If Laban finds them with anyone in Jacob's camp, what happens to that person?

answers.text: That person will be sent away

cards.question: When Jacob makes that promise, he knows Rachel has the idols.

cards.text: Jacob tells Laban to look for himself in front of their relatives. So Laban searches Jacob's tent, then the tent of Leah, Jacob's other wife, then the tents of the two maidservants, and finds nothing.

cards.question: Four tents searched and nothing found. Then Laban walks into ___'s tent.
Rachel has her father's household idols. Where has she hidden them?

answers.text: In a saddlebag she's sitting on
Under the floor of her tent
Among the sheep in the flock

cards.text: Laban searches everything in that tent. Meanwhile Rachel just sits there, right on top of the idols, like somebody with absolutely nowhere to be.
Then Rachel tells him, “Sir, do not be angry that I cannot stand up before you; for I am having my period.”

cards.question: After Rachel speaks, Laban keeps searching and finally finds his household idols.

cards.text: Laban came up empty, and now Jacob is incensed. He challenges Laban: “What is my crime?”

cards.question: After all that searching, Jacob tells Laban to put anything of Laban's he found in front of both their relatives so they can judge between them.

cards.text: Then Jacob reads Laban his whole résumé. Laban's sheep and goats haven't miscarried, he says, and he never ate the rams of Laban's flock.

cards.question: Jacob says he has been with Laban for ___ years now.
Jacob says that when wild beasts tore one of Laban's animals, Laban took the loss.

cards.text: Jacob bore that loss himself, and Laban made him pay for anything stolen, day or night. Heat by day, frost by night, sleep running from his eyes: that's not a job, friend, that's a twenty-year night shift with no break room.

cards.question: Of Jacob's twenty years with Laban, what does Jacob say fourteen of them were for?

cards.text: Six more years were for the flocks, and Laban changed his wages TEN times. At that point Jacob's not getting a paycheck, friend, he's getting a surprise.

cards.question: Jacob says that if the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, Jacob's father, hadn't been with him, how would Laban have sent him away by now?

cards.text: But God has seen his affliction and the toil of his hands, Jacob says. And last night, He rendered judgment.
Laban fires back that the daughters, the kids and the flocks are all his: “Everything you see is mine!” Friend, that's a man who lost the argument and still wants the last word.

cards.question: Then Laban asks what he can do today about his daughters and the children they've had. What does Laban propose to Jacob?

answers.text: That Jacob come back with him

cards.text: So Jacob picks out a stone and sets it up as a pillar. Then he tells his relatives, “Gather some stones.”

cards.question: Jacob's relatives gather the stones. What do they make with them?

cards.text: There by the mound, they eat. Laban calls it Jegar-sahadutha, Jacob calls it Galeed, and I'm just grateful nobody's asking ME to spell either one.

cards.question: Laban says the mound is a ___ between him and Jacob.

cards.text: That's why the place is called Galeed. It's also called Mizpah, because Laban says, “May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other.”

cards.question: Laban tells Jacob that if he mistreats Laban's daughters, God is a witness even when no one else is with them.
Besides mistreating his daughters, what else does Laban tell Jacob not to do?

cards.text: Laban points to the mound and the pillar standing between him and Jacob.

cards.question: Laban says the mound and pillar are witnesses that he won't go past them to harm Jacob, but Jacob is free to go past them to harm Laban.

cards.text: Laban calls on the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, Abraham's brother (Genesis 11:26), the God of their father, to judge between them.

cards.question: Laban has called on God to judge between him and Jacob. How does Jacob respond?

answers.text: He swears by the Fear of Isaac
He refuses to swear at all

cards.question: With the covenant made, Jacob offers a ___ on the mountain and invites his relatives to eat a meal.

cards.text: After they've eaten, they spend the night on the mountain. And remember that goodbye kiss Laban said Jacob never let him have?

cards.question: Early the next morning, Laban kisses his grandchildren and daughters and blesses them.

cards.text: Then Laban heads back home. Jacob's still got miles of road ahead, friend, and this story is NOT done.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."
He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: Card 1 already tells the baker that Rachel stole her father's household idols. When card 11 asks what Laban accuses Jacob of stealing (gods, rams or silver), the answer is already given.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "Laban says he understands" adds something Laban never says. In Genesis 31:30, Laban only states that Jacob has gone off because he longs for his father's house. He never says he understands.

"And remember that goodbye kiss Laban said Jacob never let him have?" sets up card 16 so strongly that it rules out False. The baker can tell that Laban kisses his grandchildren and daughters before the card asks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
